common_failure_modes: No list of approved maintenance tools, so any remote support program can be used.
Vendor technicians appear in maintenance records but not on any authorized list.
Maintenance accounts are shared or never disabled after the vendor leaves.
Tools the policy forbids are found installed on in-scope machines.
Nobody can say how a new tool or vendor is approved before use.

objectives.determination: tools used to conduct system maintenance are controlled
techniques used to conduct system maintenance are controlled
mechanisms used to conduct system maintenance are controlled
personnel used to conduct system maintenance are controlled

practices.title:
Ensure equipment removed for off-site maintenance is sanitized of any CUI.
Assessment Objective:
[a] equipment to be removed from organizational spaces for off-site maintenance is sanitized of any CUI.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks what happens when a device or drive leaves the building for repair. They read the procedure for off-site maintenance and look for a step that removes or sanitizes CUI before the equipment goes, and a record for each item shipped out (what it was, how it was sanitized, who did it, when). They interview the person who ships equipment out and, if any items went out in the review period, sample those records. Where a device cannot be sanitized because it is broken, they look for what was done instead (drive removed and kept, or vendor agreement covering CUI). This practice is not in the CES control signal registry; it rests on records and interviews.
common_failure_modes: Laptops go out for warranty repair with the drive still in and no sanitization step.
A sanitization step is written down but no record exists for items that actually left.
Broken devices that cannot be wiped are shipped anyway with nothing else done.
Staff who handle shipping do not know the procedure exists.

objectives.determination: equipment to be removed from organizational spaces for off-site maintenance is sanitized of any CUI

practices.title: Check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in organizational systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that diagnostic or test software brought in on media (vendor USB sticks, discs, downloaded tool kits) is scanned for malware before it touches a system that handles CUI. They read the policy for the scan requirement, look at the endpoint protection settings that scan removable drives and files on access, and ask a technician how they handle vendor media. Testing means plugging approved test media into a sampled machine, or showing the scan logs from a recent vendor visit.
common_failure_modes: Endpoint protection does not scan removable drives, or real-time scanning is turned off.
Vendor technicians run tools from their own media with no scan step.
The scan setting exists in a policy that is not assigned to the in-scope devices.
Nobody can produce a scan log for media used in a recent maintenance event.

objectives.determination: media containing diagnostic and test programs are checked for malicious code before being used in organizational systems that process, store, or transmit CUI

practices.title: Require multifactor authentication to establish non-local maintenance sessions via external network connections and terminate such connections when nonlocal maintenance is complete.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks at how outside administrators and vendors reach systems for maintenance over the internet, and checks two things: every such session needs multifactor authentication to start, and the session is ended when the work is done. They read the Conditional Access policies that cover remote and privileged access, sample a few recent remote maintenance sessions in the sign-in or remote tool logs, and ask how sessions are closed and vendor access turned off afterwards. Testing means trying to start a remote maintenance session without the second factor and checking that it fails.
common_failure_modes: MFA is required for users but the remote support tool has its own login with no second factor.
The Conditional Access policy is in report-only mode or excludes the accounts vendors use.
Vendor remote access stays always on instead of being opened per job.
Remote sessions have no idle timeout and are not closed when the work ends.
No log shows when a remote maintenance session started and ended.

objectives.determination: multifactor authentication is used to establish nonlocal maintenance sessions via external network connections
nonlocal maintenance sessions established via external network connections are terminated when nonlocal maintenance is complete

practices.title:
Supervise the maintenance activities of personnel without required access authorization.
Assessment Objective:
[a] maintenance personnel without required access authorization are supervised during maintenance activities.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks who does maintenance without normally having access to CUI systems (outside technicians, cleaning of equipment rooms, copier service) and how they are watched while they work. They read the procedure that requires an escort or supervising staff member, look at visitor or maintenance logs that name both the technician and the supervisor, and interview the people who do the supervising. Where supervision is remote (a staff member watching a shared screen), they ask how the session is watched and recorded. This practice is not in the CES control signal registry.
common_failure_modes: Outside technicians are left alone in server rooms or on admin consoles.
Logs show the technician but never name who supervised them.
Remote vendor sessions run unattended with nobody watching the screen.
Staff asked to supervise do not know what they are meant to watch for.

objectives.determination: maintenance personnel without required access authorization are supervised during maintenance activities

practices.title: Protect (i.e., physically control and securely store) system media containing CUI, both paper and digital.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that CUI on paper and on digital media (laptops, drives, USB sticks, discs, backup tapes) is kept physically under control and stored securely. They read the media protection policy, walk the spaces where CUI is handled to look at locked cabinets, safes and storage rooms, and check who holds the keys or codes. For digital CUI they look at where it is stored (the CUI sites and libraries, encrypted devices) and how it is labeled. In interviews they ask staff where they keep CUI paper at the end of the day and where CUI files may be saved. Testing means trying an unlocked drawer or a CUI library with an account that should not get in.
common_failure_modes: CUI paper is left on desks or in open trays overnight.
Storage cabinets lock but keys are shared or hang next to the cabinet.
Digital CUI is saved to personal drives or unlabeled locations outside the CUI sites.
Sensitivity labels exist in the tenant but are not applied to the libraries that hold CUI.
Staff cannot say where CUI is allowed to be stored.

objectives.determination: paper media containing CUI is physically controlled
digital media containing CUI is physically controlled
paper media containing CUI is securely stored
digital media containing CUI is securely stored

practices.title:
Limit access to CUI on system media to authorized users.
Assessment Objective:
[a] access to CUI on system media is limited to authorized users.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that only authorized people can get at CUI held on media, both files in storage and removable or portable media. They compare the list of people authorized for CUI with who can actually open CUI libraries, labeled files and encrypted devices. They read the sensitivity label settings to see whether the CUI label encrypts content and limits it to the authorized group, and sample a few labeled files to see who has rights. Testing means trying to open a labeled CUI file or library with an account that is not authorized.
common_failure_modes: The CUI label marks content but does not encrypt it or limit who can open it.
CUI libraries grant access to all staff or to guest users.
The authorized-user list and the CUI security group membership do not match.
Large parts of CUI content carry no label, so label-based access never applies.

objectives.determination: access to CUI on system media is limited to authorized users

practices.title: Sanitize or destroy information system media containing Federal Contract Information (FCI) before disposal or release for reuse.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that media holding CUI is wiped or destroyed before it is thrown away, and wiped before it is handed to someone else to reuse. They read the sanitization procedure for the methods allowed for each kind of media (paper, hard drives, solid-state drives, phones), then ask for disposal and reuse records for a sample of items: what it was, method used, who did it, when, and a destruction certificate where a vendor was used. They interview the person who handles disposal and check the wipe records for devices of departed or reassigned staff.
common_failure_modes: Old drives and laptops sit in a closet or go to recycling with no wipe or destruction record.
Devices are reissued to a new user without a wipe.
CUI paper goes in the ordinary trash instead of a shredder or locked shred bin.
A destruction vendor is used but no certificates are kept.
The wipe method is not suited to the media (a quick format on a hard drive).

objectives.determination: system media containing CUI is sanitized or destroyed before disposal
system media containing CUI is sanitized before it is released for reuse

practices.title: Mark media with necessary CUI markings and distribution limitations.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that media holding CUI carries the right CUI marking and any limit on who it may be shared with. They read the marking procedure, look at a sample of CUI documents, emails, drives and printed material for the CUI banner, designation block and any dissemination control, and check the sensitivity label settings that add headers, footers or watermarks. In interviews they ask staff how they know when and how to mark something. Testing means creating a labeled test file and checking the marking appears.
common_failure_modes: Documents carry the CUI label in metadata but no visible marking.
Removable media and printed copies holding CUI are not marked at all.
Distribution limits from the contract are never added to the marking.
Staff use old markings (FOUO, Proprietary) instead of CUI markings.
Nobody has written down which marking applies to which kind of CUI.

objectives.determination: media containing CUI is marked with applicable CUI markings
media containing CUI is marked with distribution limitations

practices.title: Control access to media containing CUI and maintain accountability for media during transport outside of controlled areas.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks two things: access to CUI media is controlled, and CUI media taken outside controlled areas is tracked while in transit. They read the media protection policy, look at the device settings that limit use of removable storage, and ask for a media checkout or transport log showing who took what, when it left, by what route or carrier and when it came back or arrived. They interview the person who sends or carries media and sample log entries against the inventory.
common_failure_modes: Anyone can copy CUI to a USB stick and walk out with it.
No log records CUI media leaving the site or arriving at its destination.
Couriers are used with no tracking or signed receipt.
The media inventory does not match what the transport log says went out.

objectives.determination: access to media containing CUI is controlled
accountability for media containing CUI is maintained during transport outside of controlled areas

practices.title:
Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of CUI stored on digital media during transport unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.
Assessment Objective:
[a] the confidentiality of CUI stored on digital media is protected during transport using cryptographic mechanisms or alternative physical safeguards.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that CUI on laptops, drives and other digital media that leave controlled areas is encrypted, or else protected by physical means that the organization has written down (a locked case carried by an authorized person, for example). They read the encryption policy and the device settings for full-disk and removable-drive encryption, check the encryption status of a sample of laptops and portable drives, and ask how staff carry media when encryption is not possible. Where encryption is used, they ask whether it is FIPS-validated.
common_failure_modes: Laptops are encrypted but USB drives and external disks are not.
The encryption policy exists but is not assigned to all in-scope devices.
Encryption is not FIPS-validated and no alternative physical safeguard is documented.
Staff ship CUI drives with no encryption and no locked container.

objectives.determination: the confidentiality of CUI stored on digital media is protected during transport using cryptographic mechanisms or alternative physical safeguards

practices.title:
Control the use of removable media on system components.	
Assessment Objective:
[a] the use of removable media on system components is controlled.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that the organization decides which removable media may be used on its systems and enforces that choice. They read the removable media rules (blocked, read-only, or allowed only for approved devices), look at the device control settings in Intune, and test a sampled machine by plugging in an unapproved USB drive. They interview staff about how they move files and how exceptions are approved.
common_failure_modes: The policy blocks removable media but no device setting enforces it.
The block applies to some devices or user groups and leaves others open.
Exceptions are granted informally and never reviewed.
Removable media is blocked on Windows but not on Mac or Linux machines in scope.

objectives.determination: the use of removable media on system components is controlled

practices.title:
Prohibit the use of portable storage devices when such devices have no identifiable owner.
Assessment Objective:
[a] the use of portable storage devices is prohibited when such devices have no identifiable owner.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that portable storage devices with no known owner cannot be used on the organization's systems. They read the rule that bans unowned devices, look at the device control settings (a full block, or an allow list tied to registered owners), and check the register of issued portable devices. Testing means plugging an unregistered device into a sampled machine and seeing it refused.
common_failure_modes: Found or giveaway USB drives can be plugged in and used.
Issued portable drives are not registered to a named owner.
The allow list is tied to device type rather than to specific registered devices.
Staff are not told what to do with a device they find.

objectives.determination: the use of portable storage devices is prohibited when such devices have no identifiable owner

practices.title:
Protect the confidentiality of backup CUI at storage locations.
Assessment Objective:
[a] the confidentiality of backup CUI is protected at storage locations.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that backup copies of CUI are kept confidential wherever they are stored. They find out where backups live (cloud vault, backup appliance, off-site tapes), read how they are encrypted and who can reach them, and compare the backup operator list with the people who can actually read or restore. They look at the backup status and a recent restore test, and ask how off-site copies are carried and stored. Testing means checking the encryption setting on the backup store and trying access with an account that should not have it.
common_failure_modes: Backups are taken but not encrypted at the storage location.
Too many people can read or restore backups, including general IT staff with no need.
Off-site tapes or drives are stored somewhere with no physical control.
Nobody knows where all the backup copies of CUI are kept.

objectives.determination: the confidentiality of backup CUI is protected at storage locations

practices.title: Limit physical access to organizational information systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorized individuals.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor first settles which spaces are in scope: every office, server room, wiring closet or lab where CUI systems or the equipment that serves them sit, plus what is inherited from the cloud provider. For each space they read the list of people allowed in and compare it with the badge or key system and with current staff. On site they walk the entry points, check that doors lock, and try to get into a restricted room without a badge or escort. They ask the facility owner how a name is added to or removed from the list, and ask a few staff which rooms they can enter.
common_failure_modes: There is no written list of who may enter each restricted space; access rests on who happens to hold a key.
People who left or changed jobs still appear in the badge system or still hold keys.
Network equipment sits in an unlocked closet or shared space even though the main office is controlled.
The organization claims everything is inherited from the cloud provider while staff still handle CUI in an office.
Doors that are meant to be locked are propped open or the lock is not working on the day of the visit.

objectives.determination: authorized individuals allowed physical access are identified
physical access to organizational systems is limited to authorized individuals
physical access to equipment is limited to authorized individuals
physical access to operating environments is limited to authorized individuals

practices.title: Protect and monitor the physical facility and support infrastructure for organizational systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks at how the building and the rooms holding CUI systems are protected (locks, alarms, window and door hardening) and how the supporting services are protected (power, cooling, cabling, network demarcation). They then look at how both are watched: alarm monitoring, cameras, guard rounds or after-hours checks, and who reviews alerts. They read alarm and monitoring records for a recent period, ask the facility owner what happens when an alarm goes off, and on site confirm that cameras and sensors point at the places the plan says they cover. Where a landlord or data center provides the protection, they ask for the agreement that says so.
common_failure_modes: Protection is described for the front door only; the equipment room, cabling and power feed are not covered.
Cameras or alarms exist but nobody reviews the footage or receives the alerts.
Protection depends on the landlord, with no agreement or report showing what the landlord does.
No monitoring record can be produced for the review period.
Support equipment such as a UPS or network panel sits where anyone in the building can reach it.

objectives.determination: the physical facility where organizational systems reside is protected
the support infrastructure for organizational systems is protected
the physical facility where organizational systems reside is monitored
the support infrastructure for organizational systems is monitored

practices.title: Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the visitor procedure to see who counts as a visitor, who may escort, and where visitors may and may not go. They examine the visitor log for a recent period and pick entries to check that each names a host and has sign-in and sign-out times. In interviews they ask reception and a few staff what they do when a visitor arrives and when they see an unescorted stranger. If allowed, the assessor arrives as a visitor and watches whether they are signed in, badged and kept with an escort.
common_failure_modes: Visitors sign in but are then left to walk the office alone.
The visitor log has missing sign-out times or no named host.
Cleaning crews, delivery staff or contractors are not treated as visitors and go unescorted.
Staff do not know what to do when they see someone without a badge.
Visitor badges look the same as staff badges, so an escort lapse is hard to spot.

objectives.determination: visitors are escorted
visitor activity is monitored

practices.title: Maintain audit logs of physical access.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks for a record of who entered the controlled spaces and when: badge system history, sign-in sheets, key logs or visitor logs. They check how long the records are kept, who can change them, and whether anyone reviews them. They pick a date and a person and ask the facility owner to pull that entry, and they compare a badge history excerpt with the staff list to look for entries by people who should no longer have access.
common_failure_modes: Only visitors are logged; staff entry to controlled rooms leaves no record.
Logs are kept for a few weeks only, so the review period cannot be shown.
Paper logs have gaps, illegible entries or pages missing.
Nobody reviews the logs, so entries by departed staff go unnoticed.
Keys are used for the equipment room and no key log exists.

objectives.determination: audit logs of physical access are maintained

practices.title: Control and manage physical access devices.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks for the inventory of physical access devices: keys, badges, fobs, door codes and lock combinations. They check that each device is assigned to a named person, that lost devices are reported and disabled, and that codes and combinations change when someone who knew them leaves. They compare issued badges and keys with the staff list, ask the facility owner how a departing person's devices are recovered, and pick a recent leaver to confirm their badge was turned off.
common_failure_modes: No inventory of keys or badges exists, or it lists devices without the person holding them.
Badges of departed staff are still active in the badge system.
Door codes or safe combinations have not changed in years, despite staff turnover.
Master or spare keys are kept in an unlocked drawer.
Lost badges are replaced without the old one being disabled.

objectives.determination: physical access devices are identified
physical access devices are controlled
physical access devices are managed

practices.title: Enforce safeguarding measures for CUI at alternate work sites.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the rules for working on CUI away from the main site, such as at home, at a customer site or while travelling: where CUI may be handled, how screens and printouts are protected, how devices are stored, and which connection methods are allowed. They then look for proof the rules are applied: signed telework agreements, device rules that apply to remote devices, and records of remote work approvals. In interviews they ask remote staff how they protect CUI at home, and they may ask one to show their setup over a video call.
common_failure_modes: Remote work happens but no written safeguards exist for alternate work sites.
The rules exist but remote staff never signed or saw them.
Staff print CUI at home with no rule on storing or destroying the printouts.
Remote staff use personal devices that are not covered by the organization's device controls.
Staff describe practices in interview, such as working in public places, that the rules forbid.

objectives.determination: safeguarding measures for CUI are defined for alternate work sites
safeguarding measures for CUI are enforced for alternate work sites

practices.title:
Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI.
Assessment Objective:
[a] individuals are screened prior to authorizing access to organizational systems 
containing CUI.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the screening procedure to see what checks are done before someone gets access to CUI systems, for example identity, right to work, references and a background check, and who decides the result. They take a sample of current account holders, including administrators and contractors, and compare the date screening finished with the date the account was created or added to CUI groups. Screening must come first. They ask HR and the security lead how screening is tracked, what happens when it is not finished, and how rescreening is handled when it is required.
common_failure_modes: Accounts were created before screening finished, with the screening record dated later.
Contractors or administrators were never screened because they came through a third party.
Screening records exist in HR but cannot be tied to the accounts the person holds.
The procedure does not say what screening is required, so adequacy cannot be judged.
The decision to grant access after screening is not recorded or names no approver.

objectives.determination: individuals are screened prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI

practices.title: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the offboarding and transfer procedure to see what happens to accounts, credentials, devices and CUI access when someone leaves or changes jobs, and how fast. They take recent leavers and movers from HR and check in the tenant that each leaver's account was disabled on time and that each mover lost access they no longer need. They look for leftover rights such as role assignments, group memberships, shared mailbox access or keys still held. They ask HR and IT how they hear about a personnel action, and they check that the tenant runs leaver and mover workflows on a schedule rather than by hand.
common_failure_modes: HR does not tell IT about leavers in time, so accounts stay active for days or weeks.
Disabled accounts still hold administrator roles or group memberships.
Transfers keep all the rights from the old job because only terminations are handled.
Shared passwords, service accounts or physical keys known to the leaver are not changed.
Leaver workflows exist in the tenant but are disabled or only run on demand.

objectives.determination: a policy and/or process for terminating system access and any credentials coincident with personnel actions is established
system access and credentials are terminated consistent with personnel actions such as termination or transfer
the system is protected during and after personnel transfer actions

practices.title: Periodically assess the risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image or reputation), organizational assets and individuals, resulting from the operation of organizational systems and the associated processing, storage or transmission of CUI.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the risk assessment procedure for a stated cycle (for example yearly, and after major changes) and a scope that names the systems handling CUI. They then look at the most recent completed assessment and the one before it, checking the dates against the stated cycle and checking that the work covers threats to operations, assets and people, with likelihood and impact rated for each risk. They interview whoever owns the assessment about how it was done, who signed it off and what changed as a result. Testing means tracing a few risks from the register back to their source, such as a scan finding or an incident, and confirming the register has been touched since the last review. CES has no automated tenant signal for this practice; it rests on the risk register, the signed annual snapshot and interviews.
common_failure_modes: No assessment cycle is written down, so there is nothing to measure the dates against.
The last completed assessment is older than the cycle the procedure states.
The scope never names the CUI systems, or describes a different environment from the SSP boundary.
The risk list is generic and rates no likelihood or impact for this organization.
The assessment was done once for the certification and the register has not been updated since.
Nobody signed the assessment off, or the person named cannot describe how it was done.

objectives.determination: the frequency to assess risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, and individuals is defined

risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, and individuals resulting from the operation of an organizational system that processes, stores, or transmits CUI is assessed with the defined frequency

practices.title: Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems and applications periodically and when new vulnerabilities affecting those systems and applications are identified.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the vulnerability scanning procedure for a stated scan cycle that covers both systems (servers, endpoints, network devices) and applications, and for what happens when a new vulnerability is announced. They compare the scan results over recent months against that cycle and compare the list of scanned devices against the asset inventory. They ask the person who runs the scanner how a newly announced vulnerability leads to an extra scan or check, and ask for an example. Testing means picking a few devices and applications from the inventory and finding them in the latest results, and picking a recent public vulnerability and seeing whether the organization checked for it. In CES the device side is read from Microsoft Defender vulnerability management; applications outside Defender's software inventory need scan reports uploaded.
common_failure_modes: The procedure gives no scan cycle, or gives one for systems but not for applications.
Scan results show gaps longer than the stated cycle.
Devices in the inventory never appear in any scan result.
Web or custom applications are never scanned; only operating systems are covered.
There is no process for checking a newly announced vulnerability before the next scheduled scan.
Scans run without credentials, so most findings on the host are missed.

objectives.determination: the frequency to scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems and applications is defined
vulnerability scans are performed on organizational systems with the defined frequency
vulnerability scans are performed on applications with the defined frequency
vulnerability scans are performed on organizational systems when new vulnerabilities are identified
vulnerability scans are performed on applications when new vulnerabilities are identified

practices.title: Remediate vulnerabilities in accordance with risk assessments.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that scan findings become a tracked list of vulnerabilities, and that the order and deadline for fixing them follow the risk rating the organization gave them (for example critical within a set number of days). They read the remediation procedure for those deadlines, then pick a sample of findings from older scans and follow each one to a fix, a later clean scan, or a recorded decision to accept or defer it, with a POA&M entry where it stays open. They interview the person who assigns the fixes about how priority is set. Testing means comparing an earlier scan with a later one to see whether the sampled findings disappeared within the stated deadlines.
common_failure_modes: Findings are left in the scanner console and never become a tracked item.
No remediation deadlines by severity are written down, so timeliness cannot be judged.
Critical findings stay open well past the stated deadline with no recorded reason.
Accepted or deferred vulnerabilities have no risk decision and no POA&M entry.
Patches are deployed but no later scan confirms the vulnerability is gone.

objectives.determination: vulnerabilities are identified
vulnerabilities are remediated in accordance with risk assessments

practices.title: Periodically assess the security controls in organizational systems to determine if the controls are effective in their application.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the security assessment policy for a stated cycle for checking whether the controls work, and then looks for the reports of the most recent assessments against that cycle. A report should say which controls were checked, how (document review, interviews, technical checks), what was found and who did the work. They interview the person responsible about how the scope is chosen and what happened with the findings. Testing means taking a few controls the last report marked effective and checking them again now. CES has no tenant signal for this practice; an AdminOps benchmark report and Defender for Cloud compliance results can support it, but a configuration report alone is not a control assessment.
common_failure_modes: No assessment cycle is written down.
The only assessment on file is the one done to prepare for certification.
A configuration or compliance-score report is offered in place of an assessment of the controls.
The report lists no findings and no method, so effectiveness cannot be judged.
Findings from the last assessment never reached the POA&M.

objectives.determination: the frequency of security control assessments is defined
security controls are assessed with the defined frequency to determine if the controls are effective in their application

practices.title: Develop and implement plans of action (e.g., POA&M) designed to correct deficiencies and reduce or eliminate vulnerabilities in organizational systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor wants a plan of action that lists each known deficiency and vulnerability, where it came from (an assessment, a scan, an incident), what will be done about it, who owns it and by when. They compare the plan against the latest assessment results and scan findings to see that nothing found is missing from it. They then pick open and closed items and look for proof of progress: a fix, a changed setting, a closure record with evidence. In interviews they ask the owner how items get onto the plan, how often it is reviewed and what happens when a date slips. Testing means checking that an item marked closed is really fixed in the system.
common_failure_modes: Findings from the last assessment or scan are missing from the plan of action.
Items have no owner, no planned action or no completion date.
Dates have slipped repeatedly with no recorded reason or new date.
Items are marked closed but the deficiency is still present in the system.
The plan is a document made once for the assessment and never updated.

objectives.determination: deficiencies and vulnerabilities to be addressed by the plan of action are identified
a plan of action is developed to correct identified deficiencies and reduce or eliminate identified vulnerabilities
the plan of action is implemented to correct identified deficiencies and reduce or eliminate identified vulnerabilities

practices.title:
Monitor security controls on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of the controls.
Assessment Objective:
[a] security controls are monitored on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued 
effectiveness of those controls.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks for a written monitoring approach: which controls are watched between full assessments, how (automated checks, log review, scan results, recurring reviews), how often, and who reviews the output. They examine recent monitoring output and look for evidence that a change for the worse was noticed and acted on. They interview the people who receive the monitoring output about what they look at and what they did with the last alert or drop. Testing means picking a control and showing that its current state is known from monitoring rather than from the last assessment. In CES, repeated assessment snapshots and drift records show changes over time, but the organization must show someone reviews them.
common_failure_modes: Monitoring is described only as the yearly assessment.
Tools produce reports or alerts that nobody is named to review.
A control dropped from effective to not met and nothing was done about it.
Monitoring covers only technical settings; process controls such as training or access reviews are never checked between assessments.

objectives.determination: security controls are monitored on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of those controls

practices.title: Develop, document and periodically update System Security Plans (SSPs) that describe system boundaries, system environments of operation, how security requirements are implemented and the relationships with or connections to other systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the system security plan from start to finish. It must describe the boundary of the CUI environment (what is in and what is out), the environment it runs in (locations, hosting, the cloud tenant, users), how each of the 110 requirements is met, any requirement the organization treats as not applicable with the approval for that, and the connections to other systems and external providers. They compare the boundary and asset list with the network diagram, the tenant and what they see on site, and compare implementation statements with what they test elsewhere in the assessment. They check the plan's version history against the update cycle it states, and interview the plan owner about how it is kept current.
common_failure_modes: The boundary is vague, or the asset list does not match the network diagram or the tenant.
Implementation statements repeat the requirement wording instead of saying how it is done here.
A requirement is treated as not applicable with no reason and no approval recorded.
Connections to external providers, cloud services or other internal systems are not listed.
No update cycle is written down, or the version history shows no update within it.
The plan describes settings that testing shows are not in place.

objectives.determination: a system security plan is developed
the system boundary is described and documented in the system security plan
the system environment of operation is described and documented in the system security plan
the security requirements identified and approved by the designated authority as non-applicable are identified
the method of security requirement implementation is described and documented in the system security plan
the relationship with or connection to other systems is described and documented in the system security plan
the frequency to update the system security plan is defined
system security plan is updated with the defined frequency

practices.title: Monitor, control and protect organizational communications (e.g., information transmitted or received by organizational information systems) at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of the information systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor starts with the boundary description and network diagram in the SSP. They expect to see the external boundary (where the system meets the internet and outside cloud services) and the key internal boundaries (for example the CUI enclave subnet, the management subnet, guest or lab networks). For each boundary they ask three questions: what watches the traffic, what decides which traffic is allowed, and what protects the traffic that crosses it. They examine firewall and network security group rules, Conditional Access policies and log settings, interview the network or cloud administrator, and test by reading a recent sample of boundary logs and checking that a blocked connection really is blocked and recorded.
common_failure_modes: Only the internet edge is described; no internal boundary is named, so the CUI systems sit on a flat network.
The diagram does not match the tenant: subnets, network security groups or public IPs exist that the diagram leaves out.
Traffic is logged at the boundary but nobody reviews the logs or acts on what they show.
Allow-any rules or broad inbound rules remain in place with no recorded reason.
Cloud services that hold CUI (mail, file sharing, Teams) are left out of the boundary picture.
Flow logging is on at the edge but not on the internal subnets the SSP calls key boundaries.

objectives.determination: the external system boundary is defined
key internal system boundaries are defined
communications are monitored at the external system boundary
communications are monitored at key internal boundaries
communications are controlled at the external system boundary
communications are controlled at key internal boundaries
communications are protected at the external system boundary
communications are protected at key internal boundaries

practices.title: Employ architectural designs, software development techniques and systems engineering principles that promote effective information security within organizational systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks the organization to show which security design ideas it has chosen and where they are written down: for example layered defenses, least privilege, segmentation of CUI, secure defaults, and how changes are reviewed. If the organization writes or scripts any software (including automation scripts and configuration code), they look for the secure development practices it follows. They then look for proof those ideas were used: architecture documents, design review records, hardening baselines and cloud security recommendation reports with follow-up. They interview the person who designs the system and, where relevant, whoever writes code. Testing means picking one design idea from the documents and finding it in the live configuration.
common_failure_modes: Principles are copied from a framework but never tied to this system, so nothing shows they were applied.
No design or architecture review happens before changes go live.
In-house scripts or code are written without any stated secure coding practice, and the SSP says none is needed.
Cloud security recommendations sit open for months with no decision recorded.
The person who designed the system cannot point to where a stated principle shows up in the configuration.

objectives.determination: architectural designs that promote effective information security are identified
software development techniques that promote effective information security are identified
systems engineering principles that promote effective information security are identified
identified architectural designs that promote effective information security are employed
identified software development techniques that promote effective information security are employed
identified systems engineering principles that promote effective information security are employed

practices.title: Separate user functionality from system management functionality.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that the organization has listed the tools and functions used to run the system (admin portals, consoles, PowerShell, server management, network device management) and keeps them apart from what ordinary users do. In practice that means administrators use separate admin accounts, admin roles are given only when needed, and admin interfaces are not reachable from ordinary user sessions. They examine the role assignment list and account naming, interview administrators about how they do admin work, and test by trying to reach an admin portal or tool from a standard user account and by checking that a sampled admin does daily work, such as email, from a separate account.
common_failure_modes: Administrators read email and browse the web with the same account that holds admin roles.
There is no list of management functions, so the assessor cannot tell what should be kept apart.
Admin roles are permanent rather than activated when needed, and many users hold them.
Standard users can open admin portals or run management tools without any block.
Shared admin accounts make it impossible to tell who did what.

objectives.determination: user functionality is identified
system management functionality is identified
user functionality is separated from system management functionality

practices.title:
Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
Assessment Objective:
[a] unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources is 
prevented.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks for how the organization stops information left behind by one user or process from being seen by the next one on shared resources: shared devices, shared drives, terminal servers, virtual desktops, printers and memory or storage that gets reused. Much of the low-level part (memory and disk reuse inside the cloud service and operating system) is handled by Microsoft and the operating system, and the assessor expects the SSP to say so. For what the organization runs itself, they examine settings such as profile clean-up on shared machines, secure print release and permissions on shared folders, interview the administrator, and test by signing in as a second user on a shared device and looking for the first user's files.
common_failure_modes: The SSP relies on the cloud provider for everything and says nothing about shared devices or shared folders the organization runs.
Shared workstations keep earlier users' profiles, downloads or cached files.
Shared folders that hold CUI are open to everyone in the organization.
Printed CUI waits in open output trays on shared printers.
Generic shared accounts are used on shared machines.

objectives.determination: unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources is prevented

practices.title: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks for the list of everything the public can reach: websites, public IP addresses, email gateways, VPN endpoints, file-sharing links and any cloud resource with a public endpoint. They compare that list with what exists in the cloud subscription and tenant. For each public component they check it sits in its own subnet or zone, physically or logically apart from the internal network, with rules that stop it from reaching internal systems directly. They interview the network or cloud administrator and test by checking the rules between the public zone and internal subnets, and by confirming that a public resource cannot open a connection to an internal one.
common_failure_modes: No list of public-facing components exists, or it misses cloud resources with public endpoints.
A public web server sits in the same subnet as internal systems.
Rules between the public zone and internal subnets allow broad traffic.
The SSP counts the host firewall on laptops as the only separation for public components.

objectives.determination: publicly accessible system components are identified
subnetworks for publicly accessible system components are physically or logically separated from internal networks

practices.title: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception (e.g., deny all, permit by exception).
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that every boundary device and host firewall starts from deny all, and that each allowed flow has a recorded business reason and an approver. They examine firewall and network security group rule sets end to end, looking for a final deny rule and for broad allow rules, and compare every allow rule with the approved exception list. They interview the network or cloud administrator about how an exception is requested and removed, and test by trying a port or protocol that is not on the list and expecting it to be refused.
common_failure_modes: The rule set ends in allow-any, or the platform default allows outbound traffic and nobody changed it.
Allow rules exist with no business reason, owner or approval date.
Exceptions are added but never reviewed or removed.
Host firewalls are on but default inbound action is left at allow on one profile.
Outbound traffic is not filtered at all; only inbound is denied by default.

objectives.determination: network communications traffic is denied by default
network communications traffic is allowed by exception

practices.title:
Prevent remote devices from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with organizational systems and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling).
Assessment Objective:
[a] remote devices are prevented from simultaneously establishing non-remote 
connections with the system and communicating via some other connection to 
resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling).
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor first asks how remote users reach the system. If they use a VPN, the assessor checks that VPN profiles send all traffic through the tunnel while connected, so a remote device cannot talk to the internet directly and to the organization at the same time. If there is no VPN and users reach cloud services directly, the assessor expects the SSP to explain this and how access is still controlled (for example Conditional Access with compliant devices and allowed locations). They examine VPN profile settings, interview the network administrator, and test by connecting a remote device and checking its routes or trying to reach an outside site without going through the tunnel.
common_failure_modes: VPN profiles leave split tunneling on for speed, with no recorded exception.
Some VPN profiles are set correctly and others, often older ones, are not.
The SSP says split tunneling is blocked but no VPN profile or setting shows it.
No VPN is used and the SSP does not explain how remote access to CUI is controlled instead.

objectives.determination: remote devices are prevented from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with the system and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling)

practices.title: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks for the list of ways CUI leaves or moves between locations: email, file sharing, web apps, VPN, remote desktop, mobile devices, removable media sent by courier. For each path they want to know what encryption protects it or, where encryption is not used, what physical safeguard does (for example a protected cable run or hand carry by a cleared courier). They examine TLS settings, mail transport and encryption rules, certificate records and label encryption, interview the administrator, and test by checking the protocol and TLS version on a sample of endpoints and sending a test message with CUI markings to an outside address to see that it is encrypted.
common_failure_modes: No list of transmission paths exists, so some paths (for example file transfer tools or older apps) are never checked.
Old TLS versions or clear-text protocols are still allowed on some services.
Outbound CUI email is not encrypted unless the user remembers to do it.
Certificates have expired or are close to it on services that carry CUI.
The SSP claims physical safeguards with no description of what they are.

objectives.determination: cryptographic mechanisms intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI are identified
alternative physical safeguards intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI are identified
either cryptographic mechanisms or alternative physical safeguards are implemented to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission

practices.title: Terminate network connections associated with communications sessions at the end of the sessions or after a defined period of inactivity.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks for a written idle period after which network connections are ended, and checks it is applied to the connections that matter: VPN tunnels, remote desktop sessions, admin sessions to servers and network devices, and cloud sign-in sessions. They check that sessions are also ended when the user logs off or disconnects, not left open. They examine VPN, remote desktop and Conditional Access session settings, interview the administrator, and test by leaving a remote session idle past the limit and confirming the connection is closed rather than just the screen locked.
common_failure_modes: No idle period is written down, or different documents give different values.
Only the screen lock is set; VPN and remote desktop connections stay open behind it.
Disconnected remote desktop sessions are kept alive on servers indefinitely.
Cloud sessions use long-lived tokens with no sign-in frequency set.

objectives.determination: a period of inactivity to terminate network connections associated with communications sessions is defined
network connections associated with communications sessions are terminated at the end of the sessions
network connections associated with communications sessions are terminated after the defined period of inactivity

practices.title: Establish and manage cryptographic keys for cryptography employed in organizational systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks where cryptography is used (disk encryption, TLS certificates, file and mail encryption, VPN, signing) and who creates and looks after the keys for each. They check keys are generated in a protected store, access to them is limited to named people and services, and there is a defined process for rotation, backup, recovery and revoking a key that may be exposed. They examine the key vault settings, key and certificate inventory and rotation records, interview the key custodian, and test by picking a key and checking its creation date, rotation history and who can use it.
common_failure_modes: No inventory of keys and certificates exists, so nobody knows what needs rotating.
Keys are kept in scripts, files or shared mailboxes instead of a protected store.
Too many people or services have rights to use or export keys.
No recovery process exists for disk encryption keys, or recovery keys are not escrowed.
There is no plan for what to do when a key may have been exposed.

objectives.determination: cryptographic keys are established whenever cryptography is employed
cryptographic keys are managed whenever cryptography is employed

practices.title:
Employ FIPS-validated cryptography when used to protect the confidentiality of CUI.
Assessment Objective:
[a] FIPS-validated cryptography is employed to protect the confidentiality of CUI.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor lists every place cryptography protects the confidentiality of CUI (laptop and server disks, removable media, mail and file encryption, VPN, TLS, mobile devices, backups) and asks for the FIPS 140 validation certificate number of the module that does the work in each place. For cloud services in GCC High they accept the provider's validation as inherited, but expect the organization's own endpoints, VPN and any other product to be shown separately. They examine certificate numbers against the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program list, interview the administrator, and test by checking a sample of devices for encryption status and the setting that puts the operating system in FIPS mode where that is needed.
common_failure_modes: Encryption is on but nobody can name the validation certificate for the module.
The SSP says everything is inherited from the cloud provider, but laptops, VPN or mobile devices are the organization's own.
A product claims to be FIPS compliant but the module is not on the validated list or the certificate is historical.
Some devices in scope are not encrypted at all.

objectives.determination: FIPS-validated cryptography is employed to protect the confidentiality of CUI

practices.title: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and provide indication of devices in use to users present at the device.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks for the list of collaborative computing devices in scope: webcams, microphones, conference room systems, smart boards and similar. For each type they check that it cannot be switched on remotely without someone present, and that it shows people nearby when it is in use (a light, an on-screen sign or a sound). They examine device settings and the inventory, interview the person who looks after the devices, and test by turning on a camera or microphone to see the indicator, and by trying a remote activation where the device supports one.
common_failure_modes: No inventory of collaborative devices, so conference room systems are missed.
Conference room systems allow remote join or auto-answer with camera on.
The indicator light can be turned off in software, or the device has none.
The camera is blocked on laptops but nothing covers microphones or room systems.

objectives.determination: collaborative computing devices are identified
collaborative computing devices provide indication to users of devices in use
remote activation of collaborative computing devices is prohibited

practices.title: Control and monitor the use of mobile code.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that the organization has decided which kinds of mobile code are allowed (for example Office macros, browser scripts, Java, PDF scripts, ActiveX) and from where, and that settings enforce that decision. They then look for monitoring: something that detects and records when blocked or suspicious mobile code arrives or runs. They examine the mobile code policy, mail attachment scanning and Office and browser settings, interview the administrator, and test by opening a document with a macro from an outside source and checking it is blocked and that the attempt is recorded.
common_failure_modes: No written decision on which mobile code is allowed, so settings cannot be judged.
Office macros from the internet are allowed to run.
Attachment scanning is on but nobody looks at what it catches.
Controls cover email only; browsers and downloads are left open.

objectives.determination: use of mobile code is controlled
use of mobile code is monitored

practices.title: Control and monitor the use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks which Voice over IP systems are in use (Teams calling, desk phones, softphones, conference bridges) and what the rules are for them: who may use them, who may be called, and whether outside federation or consumer accounts are allowed. They check settings enforce those rules, and that call activity and admin changes are logged and looked at. They examine the VoIP policy, Teams external access settings and usage or call records, interview the person who runs the phone system, and test by trying to reach a blocked external or consumer account.
common_failure_modes: No written rules for VoIP use, so the settings have nothing to be checked against.
Teams federation with any outside organization is left open by default.
A separate phone system or softphone is in use but left out of the SSP.
Call records and admin changes are kept but never reviewed.

objectives.determination: use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies is controlled
use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies is monitored

practices.title:
Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.	
Assessment Objective:
[a] the authenticity of communications sessions is protected.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks that each side of a communications session can trust it is talking to the right party and that the session cannot be taken over or replayed. They look for TLS with valid certificates on services, session tokens protected by the identity provider, and for email, sender checks such as DKIM, SPF and DMARC with spoofing protection. They examine certificate settings, mail authentication records and identity session settings, interview the administrator, and test by checking DNS records for the mail domain, confirming certificates on public services are valid, and checking that clients refuse a connection with a bad certificate.
common_failure_modes: DKIM is not turned on or DMARC is missing or set to take no action.
Services use self-signed or expired certificates and users are trained to click past warnings.
Old protocols that do not protect session authenticity are still allowed.
The SSP covers email only and says nothing about web, remote access or admin sessions.

objectives.determination: the authenticity of communications sessions is protected

practices.title:
Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest.
Assessment Objective:
[a] the confidentiality of CUI at rest is protected.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks where CUI is stored (laptops, servers, cloud file stores, mail, removable media, backups, mobile devices) and how each location keeps it confidential, usually by encryption, sometimes by tight access control and physical protection. They examine disk encryption status, label encryption settings and backup settings, interview the administrator, and test by picking a sample of devices and stores from the inventory and checking each is encrypted, including any personal or BYOD devices that may hold CUI.
common_failure_modes: No list of where CUI is stored, so some stores (old file shares, backups, USB drives) are missed.
Most laptops are encrypted but some are not, or encryption is suspended.
Backups or exports of CUI are written unencrypted.
Personal devices can sync CUI files with no label encryption or device encryption.
Sensitivity labels exist but the ones used for CUI do not apply encryption.

objectives.determination: the confidentiality of CUI at rest is protected

practices.title: Identify, report and correct information and information system flaws in a timely manner.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the flaw remediation procedure for three stated time frames: how soon flaws must be found, how soon they must be reported to the people who fix them, and how soon they must be fixed, usually by severity. They then take a sample of devices and recent vulnerabilities and compare the date each flaw was published or detected with the date it was reported and the date it was patched or mitigated. In interviews they ask the patch owner how new flaws reach them and what happens when a fix is late. Testing means tracing one recent critical vulnerability from detection to closure. CES's own tenant signal for this practice only confirms that device compliance policies exist; it does not show that the time frames were met, so timing rests on vulnerability records and tickets.
common_failure_modes: The procedure says patches are applied 'promptly' or 'regularly' with no number of days.
Time frames exist for fixing flaws but nothing says how soon they must be found or reported.
Vulnerability scans cover workstations only; servers, network devices or cloud workloads are left out.
Sampled critical vulnerabilities stayed open past the stated deadline with no exception or POA&M entry.
Flaws are fixed but there is no dated record showing when they were reported to the fixer.

objectives.determination: the time within which to identify system flaws is specified
system flaws are identified within the specified time frame
the time within which to report system flaws is specified
system flaws are reported within the specified time frame
the time within which to correct system flaws is specified
system flaws are corrected within the specified time frame

practices.title: Provide protection from malicious code at appropriate locations within organizational information systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the system integrity policy and the system description to find where malicious code protection is meant to run, typically endpoints, servers, email, and file storage or other entry and exit points. They then check that protection is turned on at each of those places: device antivirus settings, email attachment scanning and cloud file scanning. They interview the administrator about how a new device or service gets covered. Testing means dropping a harmless test file (such as the EICAR string) on a sampled device and through email and confirming it is caught. CES reads the Intune Defender antivirus settings for this practice; email and file-storage protection are not read by a CES tenant signal and need uploaded configuration.
common_failure_modes: The locations that need protection were never written down, so coverage cannot be judged.
Antivirus is installed on workstations but servers, virtual machines or Macs are not covered.
Email attachments or cloud file storage are not scanned even though they are named entry points.
Real-time protection can be switched off by users, or cloud-delivered protection is disabled.
A test file placed on a sampled device is not detected or blocked.

objectives.determination: designated locations for malicious code protection are identified
protection from malicious code at designated locations is provided

practices.title: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor looks for a written procedure that names the sources of security alerts and advisories the organization follows (for example CISA alerts and the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, vendor bulletins such as Microsoft's monthly security updates, and the security console's own recommendations), who reviews them, how often, and what kinds of action follow. They examine evidence that the sources are actually received and read, and pick one or two recent advisories that applied to the organization to see what was done and when. In interviews they ask the reviewer how the last relevant advisory was handled. CES reads Microsoft Secure Score and its recommendations with dates; outside advisories such as CISA bulletins are not read by any CES signal and need uploaded records.
common_failure_modes: No named sources of advisories; staff say they 'keep up with the news'.
Alerts arrive in a mailbox nobody owns or checks on a set schedule.
Response actions are not defined, so there is no way to tell whether the right thing was done.
A recent advisory that clearly applied was never assessed or acted on.
Actions were taken but nothing records which advisory prompted them or when.

objectives.determination: response actions to system security alerts and advisories are identified
system security alerts and advisories are monitored
actions in response to system security alerts and advisories are taken

practices.title:
Update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available.	
Assessment Objective:
[a] malicious code protection mechanisms are updated when new releases are available.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor checks how antivirus engines and signature definitions are kept current: the update setting, how often it runs, and who watches for devices that stop updating. They examine the configured update interval and a device health report for a sample of devices, comparing each device's signature and engine version with the current release from the vendor. In interviews they ask the administrator how they would notice a device that has not updated. CES reads the Intune Defender signature update interval and expects it to be 24 hours or less unless the organization sets a different value.
common_failure_modes: Updates are configured, but sampled devices show signature versions days or weeks old.
Devices not enrolled in Defender for Endpoint or Intune are never updated or checked.
No one reviews update health, so stale devices go unnoticed.
Engine or platform versions are left behind even though signature definitions update.

objectives.determination: malicious code protection mechanisms are updated when new releases are available

practices.title: Perform periodic scans of the information system and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened or executed.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor reads the policy for how often full or quick malware scans must run, then checks the configured scan schedule and the scan history on a sample of devices to see that scans actually ran at that frequency. They also check that files are scanned in real time when downloaded, opened or run, including files from email, the web and removable media. Testing means downloading or copying a harmless test file on a sampled device and confirming it is caught at that moment. CES reads the Intune Defender scan schedule, scan type and real-time monitoring settings; the configured schedule shows intent, so the assessor still asks for scan history to show the scans ran.
common_failure_modes: The policy names no scan frequency, or the configured schedule does not match it.
Scheduled scans are set to user-defined, so users can skip or change them.
Scan history shows sampled devices with no completed scan in the stated period.
Real-time scanning is off for some devices or does not cover file activity.
Files from removable media or network shares are not scanned when opened.

objectives.determination: the frequency for malicious code scans is defined
malicious code scans are performed with the defined frequency
real-time malicious code scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed are performed

practices.title: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor asks how the organization watches its systems for attacks: which tools raise alerts (for example Defender XDR, Entra ID Protection, Sentinel, firewalls), who reviews them, and how quickly. They check that monitoring covers both traffic coming in (email, web, remote access, inbound network flows) and traffic going out (outbound connections, data leaving by email or web), not only endpoints. They examine alert and incident records for a recent period and pick a few to trace from alert to triage. In interviews they ask the person on watch what they did with the last real alert. CES checks that the security alert, risk detection and Secure Score feeds were all read and healthy in the window; that shows the feeds operate, not that inbound and outbound traffic is covered, which rests on network and email logging.
common_failure_modes: Alerts are generated but nobody is assigned to review them, or review happens only after an incident.
Monitoring covers endpoints only; network traffic in and out of the boundary is not logged or watched.
Outbound traffic is not monitored at all, so data leaving the system would go unseen.
A monitoring feed has been broken or disconnected for weeks without anyone noticing.
An outside monitoring provider is used but its scope and hand-off to the organization are not written down.

objectives.determination: the system is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks
inbound communications traffic is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks
outbound communications traffic is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks

practices.title: Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems.
practices.what_assessor_does: The assessor first looks for a written statement of what authorized use is, such as an acceptable use policy or rules of behavior, so that unauthorized use has something to be measured against. They then ask how unauthorized use is spotted: risky sign-ins, unusual account activity, use outside approved locations or hours, and alerts for access being gained, kept or abused. They examine detection records for a recent period and pick a few to see that each one was looked at and given an outcome.
